about: Reference clips for scripts/accent-judge.ts's calibration: the same sentences read by British voices (ElevenLabs Alice; George) and an American one (OpenAI coral with no accent instruction). Copied from the accent audit (playtest/voice-picker/audit.md; its raw takes are in the gitignored playtest/runs/voice-picker/audit). Each clip lists its target words per feature: bath (the BATH vowel), r (an r after a vowel, before a consonant or a pause), flap (a t between vowels). `anchors` are the pairs of clips the r and flap questions compare against (they are not calibration items). A reference word is listed only where it carries its accent's form: the accent audit's acoustics (playtest/runs/voice-picker/audit/measures.json) put coral's "four" at F3 0.99 of her usual (no r), so it is left out.

refs.text: Hello, ninja! Today I'm going to show you how to read a brand new word. Are you ready?
Can you find the car? It's by the grass, next to the bath.
Let's say it the slow way first, then the fast way. Brilliant, you did it!
Say mat slowly. Now say it fast.
Water, butter, tomato, dance, can't, half past four.
Once upon a time, on an island far across the sea, grew the World Flower.
Fast or slow, it's the same word. When I say it slowly, I can hear its sounds.
Star... fish. Tap the rabbit, and say them fast.
Which class are you in? Tap your class.
The middle sound comes after the first sound, and before the last sound.
Ask a grown-up to help you type your name, then tap the green tick.
How far shall we jump? Ask a grown-up to help you choose.
Welcome to Shadow Castle. Don't worry, I'm right beside you.
Long ago, on the Island of Sounds, there grew a magic World Flower.
The World Flower has gone dark. Now nobody can read!
You did it, Super Ninja! Every petal is back on the World Flower. The whole island can read and spell again!

flap.why: The flap is judged ABX: Alice's British "Water." and coral's flapped one (in a fresh order each vote), then the clip. Asked directly, the judge called coral's flaps British in 8 of 15 votes; against these two it called 29 of 30 flaps in other voices (macOS Samantha, Sensei's shipped film_5 and finale) American and 59 of 60 British t's (macOS Daniel, Sensei's sensei-6 and film_2) British (27 Sep).

r.why: The r is judged ABX too, against Alice's British "Bird." and coral's r-coloured one. Asked directly, it was unsure of a British word-final r said alone ("Car." 2 of 4 British, "Four." 3 of 4); against these two it called all 24 votes on British r-words in other voices (Sensei's shipped w_car, w_her, film_1, the Baron's baron-1, macOS Daniel) British and 18 of 20 on American ones (Sensei's shipped w_bird and finale, macOS Samantha, the Baron's baron-1 take 3) American (27 Sep).
